findings.title: Possible collision with Falconridge Logistics WLL: GCC logistics analytics non-compete for Protected Customers
findings.impact: Potentially collides with the Falconridge non-compete commitment (live through September 2029) if Cargoline is a Protected Customer, making the representation in Clause 8.1 untrue.
readings: Reading 1: Cargoline Shipping WLL or its Affiliates are listed in Schedule 4 of the Falconridge agreement, bringing the services under the Falconridge non-compete commitment.
Reading 2: Neither Cargoline Shipping WLL nor its Affiliates are listed in Schedule 4, so the Falconridge non-compete restriction does not apply to this agreement.

citations.quote: 8.1 The Contractor represents that, as at the date of this Agreement, neither it nor any of its Affiliates is subject to any contractual restriction that would prevent or restrict it from providing the Services to the Client

during the term of this Agreement and for twenty-four (24) months after its expiry or termination, the Supplier shall not, and shall procure that its Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, provide Logistics Analytics Services to any Protected Customer anywhere in the Territory, whether as contractor, subcontractor, partner or adviser
Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, including any parent, subsidiary or sister company wherever incorporated

Logistics Analytics Services**" means fleet utilisation, route optimisation, warehouse performance, port-turnaround, freight demand forecasting and similar data analytics or data engineering services for freight, shipping, warehousing or logistics operations
Protected Customer**" means each person listed in Schedule 4, and any of its Affiliates

findings.counterPosition: Verify Schedule 4 of the Falconridge MSA with counsel to confirm whether Cargoline Shipping WLL is a Protected Customer, and modify Clause 8.1 to acknowledge existing affiliate commitments.

findings.title: Wrong AtliQ entity: Inc instead of Pvt Ltd
findings.impact: Names AtliQ Inc, but the client is in Bahrain: AtliQ Inc serves US clients only, so this should be AtliQ Pvt Ltd. The entity decides who invoices, the tax regime and the bank account; a mismatch caused two payment delays in 2025.

citations.quote: ATLIQ INC, a corporation incorporated in the State of Delaware, USA

findings.standard: AtliQ Inc contracts with US clients only; AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd with everyone else.
findings.counterPosition: Name AtliQ Pvt Ltd in the parties clause, invoicing clause and signature block.

findings.title: Immediate termination and fee clawback for conflict of interest
findings.impact: AtliQ risks being forced to refund all fees collected for completed work if any contractual restriction arises during the agreement term.

citations.quote: If such a restriction exists or arises, the Client may terminate this Agreement immediately and recover all amounts paid

findings.standard: On any termination for convenience AtliQ is paid for all work done, including work in progress. Notice is mutual. Client contracts: reasonable notice (typically 30+ days). Freelancer / vendor agreements: a mutual short exit (about 15 days, as with Rohan Iyer) is AtliQ's standard and fair to both sides.
findings.counterPosition: Delete the right to recover all amounts paid and specify that upon any termination AtliQ shall be paid for all services performed up to the termination date.

findings.title: Governing law: laws of the Kingdom of Bahrain
findings.impact: AtliQ's position is Indian law for AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd. Client law has been accepted before to win a deal (DIFC, English, Singapore): a judgment call, not a blocker.

citations.quote: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Bahrain

findings.standard: Indian law for Pvt Ltd; US law for Inc.
findings.counterPosition: Laws of India; arbitration seated in India or a neutral seat.

hits.heading: DELAY AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES
hits.label: standard
hits.labelNote: Origin of the LD playbook: 0.5% of milestone/week, 5% cap, client delays excluded (Mar 2025)
hits.text:
7.1 If the Service Provider fails to complete a Milestone by the agreed date for reasons solely attributable to the Service Provider, the Service Provider shall pay liquidated damages at the rate of 0.5% (half percent) of the Milestone Fee of the delayed Milestone for each complete week of delay.

7.2 The aggregate liquidated damages in respect of any Milestone shall not exceed 5% (five percent) of the Milestone Fee of that Milestone.

7.3 No liquidated damages shall be payable where the delay is caused by the Client, including delayed access to data or systems, delayed review of Deliverables, or changes in scope, or by a Force Majeure event.

7.4 The Parties agree that the liquidated damages are a genuine pre-estimate of loss and shall be the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for delay.
hits.differs: Worse for AtliQ than Acme Retail Group: same 0.5% weekly rate capped at 5%, but lacks Acme's explicit exclusions for client-caused delays.

hits.heading: DELAY AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES
hits.label: accident
hits.labelNote: Signed on a phone in 4 minutes: 1%/day uncapped LDs, no client-delay exclusion, group set-off, English law on a US entity. Cost $9k + $14.2k legal
hits.text:
9.1 If the Supplier fails to achieve any Key Date, the Supplier shall pay to the Customer liquidated damages in the amount of one per cent (1%) of the Contract Value for each day or part day by which the relevant Key Date is missed.

9.2 Liquidated damages under clause 9.1 shall be payable in addition to any other right or remedy available to the Customer under this Agreement or at law, and the Customer may deduct such liquidated damages from any sums due to the Supplier.

9.3 The Supplier acknowledges that the liquidated damages set out in this clause 9 are proportionate to the Customer's legitimate interest in the timely delivery of the Services.
hits.differs: Better for AtliQ than Brightwater Insurance Inc: 0.5% per week capped at 5% of milestone fee, versus 1% of total contract value per day uncapped.

10.1 The Supplier shall use all reasonable endeavours to achieve each Milestone by the date set out in the relevant SOW.

10.2 Each Deliverable shall be subject to acceptance testing by the Client within ten (10) Business Days of delivery against the acceptance criteria in the SOW. Deliverables not rejected in writing within that period shall be deemed accepted.
